title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, timeouts
author: Avery Chen
body:
Context and motivation: The continuous batcher scheduler has been a source of tail-latency variability under mixed workload patterns. We observed two classes of issues in production canaries and incident traces: (1) starvation of small, latency-sensitive requests when larger requests dominate the queue; (2) indefinite queueing for requests that wait on a KV cache miss combined with upstream stalls. This PR tunes the scheduler to provide predictable queueing fairness, detect and prevent starvation, and add configurable timeouts/backpressure to avoid unbounded queued work.

Summary of changes (commits):
- c1: introduce fairness tokens and per-priority queueing buckets; amortize scheduling decisions to avoid O(n) scans in hot paths (pkg/continuous-batcher/fairness.go, scheduler.go)
- c2: add starvation detector and escalation policy that promotes starved requests and emits metrics (timeout_policy.go, queue.go)
- c3: implement request-level queueing timeouts and backpressure hooks for KV-cache miss paths; expose config knobs in defaults.yaml
- c4: add unit + integration tests for queueing fairness, starvation scenarios, and canary perf script updates (scheduler_test.go, run.sh)

What changed (high-level):
- Scheduler: replaced a single FIFO queue with multiple priority buckets and a lightweight weighted round-robin allocator that enforces max-consecutive-serves per bucket to ensure fairness across priorities. The allocator avoids expensive global scans by maintaining a small ring of active buckets. (pkg/continuous-batcher/scheduler.go)
- Fairness: introduced a fairness token system where each request carries a token weight derived from priority and request age; the scheduler uses token accounting to prevent large-batch abrasion of small requests. Tokens are cheap integers to keep hot-path fast. (pkg/continuous-batcher/fairness.go)
- Starvation prevention: a background detector tracks per-bucket queue age percentiles and promotes requests that exceed starvation thresholds. Promotion is bounded and observable; promotions emit events for tracing. (pkg/continuous-batcher/queue.go, timeout_policy.go)
- Timeouts/backpressure: added configurable queueing_timeouts and kv_miss_backpressure_timeout. On expiry the scheduler will either fail fast with a clear error code or enqueue a low-cost placeholder that triggers a delayed retry, depending on policy. Defaults are conservative and opt-in for private deployments. (configs/batcher/defaults.yaml, docs/continuous-batcher.md)
- Observability: new metrics and traces: batcher.queue_time_seconds (histograms by priority), batcher.starvation_promotions_total, batcher.promoted_requests_latency_seconds, and trace hooks for promotion events. Updated observability/metrics/batcher.yaml.

Files changed (small illustrative snippets):
- pkg/continuous-batcher/scheduler.go: added bucket ring and allocator loop; critical path remained ~O(1) via atomic counters.
- pkg/continuous-batcher/fairness.go: FairnessToken struct (token:int, priority:int, created_at:time) and token accounting helpers.
- pkg/continuous-batcher/timeout_policy.go: new policy type with YAML-bound fields: queue_timeout_ms, kv_backpressure_ms, promotion_threshold_ms.
- docs/continuous-batcher.md: new section describing config knobs and migration guidance.

Testing and CI:
- Local unit tests added and passing (scheduler_test.go covers fairness, promotion, timeout fallthrough).
- Perf canary: cmd/perf-canary/run.sh updated to exercise mixed small/large workloads and KV-miss scenarios. Canary runs on a dev cluster showed 20-35% reduction in P99 latency for small requests in mixed workloads and eliminated indefinite queue growth in KV-miss tests.
- CI history: initial run flagged a data race in queue.go (unit-tests: fail). I addressed the race by converting a map+lock into a small fixed-size array with atomics and re-ran tests. Subsequent CI runs: lint: pass, unit-tests: pass, integration-canary: pass, e2e: pass. Final ci_status is pass.

Review conversation (high-level):
- Luca Martinez (reviewer): "Can we avoid allocations in the promotion hot-path? please benchmark that promotion doesn't regress hot-path latency."
- Author (Avery): "Promotion uses a preallocated slab and only writes a single atomic flag in the hot-path; added microbenchmark in scheduler_test.go that shows <1% overhead on our 99th-percentile microbench workload. Included results in the PR description."
- Priya Nair: "Need explicit metrics for how often promotions happen and how many get retried. Also make sure timeouts map to clear error codes upstream so SDKs can surface them."
- Author: "Added batcher.starvation_promotions_total and promoted_requests_latency_seconds. Timeout error codes are mapped to BATCHER_QUEUE_TIMEOUT and KV_BACKPRESSURE_TIMEOUT; documented in docs/continuous-batcher.md and SDKs will be able to map these strings to transient error classes."
- Jordan Blake: "What about effect on autoscaler? Promoting requests could temporarily increase concurrency; please ensure autoscaler is still stable."
- Author: "Autoscaler signals unchanged; promotion only changes scheduling order and has bounded promotions per window. Updated a note in configs/defaults.yaml and added a canary which includes autoscaler stability checks."
- Follow-up: small nits about config naming, addressed in a single follow-up commit.

Migration notes and rollout plan:
- Defaults are conservative; feature gated via configs/batcher/defaults.yaml. Rolling to Hosted API uses a staged rollout: start with 10% hosts in canary pool -> 50% -> global. Dedicated and Private customers can opt into new knobs with guidance in docs.
- Observability: dashboards updated; recommend enabling batcher.* metrics before enabling global rollout.

Release notes: "Improve continuous-batcher scheduler fairness and stability: introduce priority buckets, token-based fairness, starvation detection and promotion, and configurable queue/KV timeouts. Reduces small-request P99 in mixed workloads and prevents unbounded queue growth on KV-miss spikes."

Merge outcome: Squash-merged after approvals from Luca and Priya and green CI. Post-merge, a small hotfix (PR 247814) adjusted a default timeout value after canary telemetry; that fix was non-functional and merged the following day.

Notes for follow-up work:
- Expose per-customer tuning presets (low-latency vs high-throughput) in the Console.
- Add adaptive timeout tuning based on observed KV latency distribution.
- Investigate integrating admission control hooks with Dedicated autoscaler to coordinate promotions and capacity signals.

Related PRs and historical context: builds on previous continuous-batcher scheduler tuning PRs (see similar PRs in repo; this PR consolidates fairness and timeout work items tracked under ENG-4621).
